mentl/f92f978:
The stamp called for giving the lowering scope a way to declare a config
slot. Reading the artifact improved the design before a byte changed: no
new op is needed, because ls_enter_frame already resolves a name in
captures to RUpval(slot). Wrapping the init lowering in a frame whose
captures are the config names should have given the nested case the same
lowering the top-level case hand-builds — same slot numbering, same
handle — while deleting lower_state_init's special case into the general
resolver.

It measured worse. m3 trapped. Probing the candidate wheel directly: the
bare program compiled fine, the nested case was unchanged, and the
direct case — which worked before at exit 10 — had regressed to a trap.
So the frame was never consulted for these lowerings, and deleting the
special case removed the only mechanism that worked. Reverted whole.

Banked so the next attempt does not re-read it: ls_resolve searches
frame.captures and returns RUpval(cap_idx); ls_enter_frame is a plain
push; and the install path does reach the changed function, since
lookup_handler_state_inits_of calls lower_state_field_inits directly.
Every link checks out and the chain still fails.

The lesson is the day's second: I guessed four times this iteration — the
capture-read class, the value 1024, "state inits are never judged", and
now the frame — and the artifact refused each one. A chain whose links
each verify and whose whole still fails is a wrong model, not a wrong
link, and the answer to that is an instrument. The next probe is one
print of config_names and the resolution verdict at the init's VarRef.
No third design before it exists.
mentl/f911df1:
The hole is the gradient's syntactic absence marker — the developer's
write-mode surface for "no current selection here; gradient, propose."

Read-mode (cursor at finished code) and write-mode (cursor at ??) are
the same coin: both invoke Mentl's continuous proof-search at the
position. The hole isn't a separate mode; it's the syntactic form
that says "no candidate here yet" rather than "alternatives to what's
there." Same Synth tentacle, same constraint space, same proof
discipline — different surface presentation depending on whether the
slot is filled.

bits/f9f8329:
Companion to the UX audit. Deliberately not a task list for every
milestone: a plan written months ahead of use is re-derived from the code
anyway. What it carries instead is the part that does not survive that:
the decisions that propagate, the places where the obvious implementation
is wrong, and the order that avoids rework.

Three architects reviewed a longer draft against the source and returned
45 grounded corrections. Five were load-bearing and are verified here
against the code: flip cannot be a draw-time mirror because pass samples
are stage coords and the local/world transform ignores it; a drag commits
a CAST and would silently undo a layer reorder; pin indices are positions
six call sites pair by, so removal must null a slot rather than compact;
the service worker cache name is a constant in a static file, so every
installed phone would keep the old shell forever; and the render proof
never loads the stage component, so it cannot prove a UI split.

Also reorders the roadmap: foundations split in two, the recipe-v1 engine
work splits out of the halo milestone, the cast sheet moves after the
halo, and audio file import moves into the first milestone.

No product code changes.
